architecture_decisions.recommendation: Extracted after hook execution into a dedicated function with error collection and controlled re-throwing behavior
architecture_decisions.rationale: The original implementation had after hooks running inline after AST traversal, which meant if an error occurred during traversal, after hooks would never execute. This broke the invariant that before-after hook pairs should always complete together. By extracting runAfterHooks() and calling it from resetStateAfterError(), we guarantee after hooks run even when errors occur elsewhere.
alternatives_considered: Wrapping the entire lintFileImpl function in try/catch
Adding error handling to each individual hook call site
Using a finally block in the main linting function

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Ensured plugin state consistency by always running after hooks during error recovery
architecture_decisions.rationale: Plugins using createOnce API often maintain internal state across before/after hooks. If a before hook runs but the corresponding after hook doesn't (due to errors), the plugin's state becomes inconsistent for subsequent files. The resetStateAfterError() function now calls runAfterHooks(false) to clean up state while swallowing errors to prevent cascading failures.
alternatives_considered: Requiring plugins to implement their own error recovery
Tracking which before hooks ran and only running matching after hooks

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Replaced simple error test fixtures with comprehensive scenario-based testing
architecture_decisions.rationale: The old test fixtures (lint_after_hook_error, lint_before_hook_error) only tested isolated error cases. The new createOnce_hook_errors fixture tests all error scenarios (before, during visit, after) and verifies that after hooks still run for unaffected rules. This ensures the invariant holds across the entire plugin ecosystem.
alternatives_considered: Keeping the old test fixtures and adding new ones
Creating unit tests instead of integration tests
Testing only the most common error scenario

architecture_decisions.recommendation: Added shouldThrowIfError parameter to control error propagation in after hooks
architecture_decisions.rationale: During normal execution, errors in after hooks should propagate to the user. During error recovery (resetStateAfterError), errors should be swallowed to prevent masking the original error. The boolean parameter provides explicit control over this behavior, making the function's contract clear.
alternatives_considered: Always throwing errors from after hooks
Never throwing errors from after hooks
Using different functions for normal vs error recovery scenarios

tickets.title: Ensure after hooks always execute for createOnce plugins
tickets.description: Refactor lint.ts to guarantee that when a before hook runs, its corresponding after hook will always execute, even when errors occur during AST visitation or in other rules' hooks. This maintains plugin state consistency.

tickets.title: Create comprehensive test for hook error scenarios
tickets.description: Replace simple error test fixtures with a comprehensive test that validates after hook execution across all error scenarios (errors in before hooks, during AST visitation, and in after hooks). The test verifies that unaffected rules still have their after hooks run.

implementation_summary:
The implementation addresses a critical issue in the oxlint plugin system where after hooks could fail to execute when errors occurred during AST traversal or in other rules' hooks. This broke the invariant that before-after hook pairs should always complete together, potentially leaving plugin state inconsistent.

The core change extracts after hook execution into a dedicated runAfterHooks() function that collects errors from individual hooks and optionally re-throws them. This function is called both during normal execution (where errors should propagate) and from resetStateAfterError() (where errors should be swallowed to prevent cascading failures). The resetStateAfterError() function now guarantees after hooks run even when the main linting process fails, ensuring plugin state is properly cleaned up.

To validate this behavior, the implementation replaces two simple error test fixtures with a comprehensive test suite. The new createOnce_hook_errors fixture tests all error scenarios: errors in before hooks, during AST visitation, and in after hooks. It uses deterministic file ordering (single-threaded mode) and carefully sequenced rules to verify that unaffected rules still have their after hooks executed. The test plugin maintains event tracking across files to demonstrate that plugin state remains consistent even when errors occur in some rules.
